articles.title: Concomitant cartilage restoration does not demonstrate consistent additional clinical benefit in medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Duru DO, Wade D, Bouchard MD, Vivekanantha P, Malik SS, Skelley NW, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction with reported cartilage lesions
articles.outcomes: Pain and function scores (KOOS Pain, Kujala, IKDC); complication rates
articles.take_home: Medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction significantly improves pain and function regardless of whether cartilage damage is also treated surgically. Adding cartilage restoration did not provide additional clinical benefit and was associated with higher complication rates.

articles.title: Changes in sex distribution in Achilles tendon rupture literature over 74 years: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Potter MN, Mlecko J, Christensen M, Aufwerber S, Katz SE, Pohlig RT, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of 74 years of Achilles tendon rupture literature
articles.population: Studies of people with primary complete Achilles tendon rupture
articles.outcomes: Sex distribution trends over time; percentage of female participants in studies; proportion of studies reporting sex-disaggregated data
articles.take_home: Over the past 74 years, the proportion of women in Achilles tendon rupture studies has gradually increased from around 7% to 39%, but men still make up about 81% of participants overall. Most studies do not report separate results for men and women, which limits our understanding of whether injury patterns and outcomes differ between sexes.

articles.title: Anterior open wedge high tibial osteotomy for slope correction as a successful method in PCL insufficiency-Radiological and clinical results of a cohort study.
articles.authors: Dickschas J, Sendner T, Schubert I, Simon M, Neumaier M
articles.population: Patients with chronic posterior cruciate ligament insufficiency and reduced posterior tibial slope
articles.outcomes: Lysholm knee score improved from 59.0 to 83.0 points (p=0.0002); Tegner activity score improved from 3.0 to 5.3 (p=0.0004); 8 patients reported satisfactory knee stability; no patients needed further PCL surgery
articles.take_home: A surgical technique that increases the slope of the tibia improved knee function and stability in patients with chronic PCL damage who had a flat tibial slope. Most patients felt their knee was more stable after the operation, though their function did not fully return to pre-injury levels.

articles.title: The association between body mass index, age and severity of musculoskeletal injuries sustained during high school contact sports: A 15-year epidemiological study.
articles.authors: Bajaj P, Workman C, Angileri H, Watson S, Cho S, Tanenbaum J, et al.
articles.population: High school athletes participating in boys' and girls' soccer, basketball, wrestling and boys' football
articles.sample_size: 33,486 musculoskeletal injuries reported (weighted estimate 11,068,855 injuries nationwide)
articles.outcomes: Injury severity measured by time to return to pre-injury activity; associations between body mass index, age and recovery time
articles.take_home: Neither body mass index nor age were found to be clinically useful predictors of how long high school athletes take to recover from musculoskeletal injuries in contact sports. Although some statistical associations were found, the differences were too small to be meaningful in practice.

articles.title: Protocol for Novel Perioperative Optimization of Obese Osteoarthritic Patients pending Total Knee Replacement with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (NPO-OOPS-TKR) : a pilot randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Lau LCM, Lui TWD, Wen C, Zhu L, Lin S, Leung TKC, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 40 to 80 years with obesity (BMI ≥27 kg/m²) awaiting primary total knee replacement, with focus on Asian population
articles.outcomes: Primary outcomes: feasibility (recruitment, adherence, tolerability, retention). Exploratory outcomes: pain, body weight, patient-reported outcomes, perioperative complications
articles.take_home: This is a pilot study to test whether a weight-loss medication called semaglutide can be safely given before and after knee replacement surgery in obese older adults. The study will determine if a larger trial is feasible and whether the medication might reduce surgery complications and improve recovery.

articles.title: Similar patient-reported outcomes 6 months after unicompartmental and total knee replacement for osteoarthritis: a prospective cohort study of 60,145 patients from the Australian Orthopaedic Association National Joint Replacement Registry.
articles.authors: Fidler HL, Kiroff GK, Du P, Ackerman IN, Oakey H, Lewis PL
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee replacement surgery for osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Oxford Knee Scores, EQ-5D-5L quality of life scores, knee pain rating, patient satisfaction, and patient-perceived change at 6 months after surgery
articles.take_home: Unicompartmental and total knee replacement produced very similar improvements in pain, function and quality of life 6 months after surgery, with no meaningful difference between the two procedures from the patient's perspective. Patients having the smaller unicompartmental procedure reported slightly higher satisfaction, but the overall clinical benefits were equivalent.

articles.title: Patient Satisfaction and Outcomes at a Mean 11-Year Follow-Up Following Total Hip Arthroplasty with Subtrochanteric Osteotomy for Dislocated Hips After Schanz Osteotomy.
articles.authors: Fujii M, Kawano S, Ueno M, Oba Y, Sonohata M, Morimoto T
articles.population: Patients with chronically dislocated hips (Crowe IV dislocation) after Schanz osteotomy who underwent total hip arthroplasty with subtrochanteric osteotomy
articles.sample_size: 73 patients (93 hips); 55 patients (71 hips) completed satisfaction questionnaires
articles.outcomes: Hip function score improved from median 49 to 86 at 11 years; 89% implant survival at 10 and 20 years; 90% of patients satisfied with their outcome
articles.take_home: Total hip replacement with subtrochanteric osteotomy significantly improved hip function and patient satisfaction in this group, with most implants lasting 10 years or more. Patients who needed walking aids before surgery were more likely to have worse outcomes and lower satisfaction.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Periprosthetic Joint Infection Rates After Total Hip Arthroplasty Across Facility Types: A Single Institution Study.
articles.authors: Baek G, Baidya J, Huang R, Garemani R, Smith EB, Saxena A
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary elective total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection rates and predictors of infection
articles.take_home: Hip replacement surgery had similar infection rates whether performed in tertiary hospitals, community hospitals, specialist orthopaedic hospitals, or ambulatory surgical centres. Surgeons can safely perform hip replacements in various outpatient settings without increasing the risk of infection.

articles.title: Fast fix or false hope? Polyethylene exchange in unstable primary unconstrained total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Hanusrichter Y, Gebert C, Dudda M, Hardes J, Grimberg A, Koller D, et al.
articles.population: Patients with unconstrained primary total knee arthroplasty who underwent polyethylene exchange for secondary instability
articles.outcomes: Re-revision rate (any subsequent revision procedure); risk factors for failure; influence of secondary patellar resurfacing and timing of polyethylene exchange
articles.take_home: Polyethylene exchange can work for mild instability after knee replacement, particularly when done within two years of the original surgery and when patellar resurfacing is also performed. However, instability that appears early after the primary operation may indicate more serious underlying problems that need more extensive revision surgery.

articles.title: Preoperative Pneumonia and Its Association With Periprosthetic Joint Infection and Postoperative Complications After Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Parmar RP, Alhankawi AR, Holle AM, Verhey JT, Van Schuyver P, Tarabichi S, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national administrative claims database with matched controls
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty or total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: THA cohort: 14,607 matched pairs; TKA cohort: 6,271 matched pairs
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection and other postoperative medical and surgical complications
articles.take_home: Most pneumonias before hip or knee replacement surgery do not increase infection risk, but certain types do: Staphylococcal pneumonia within three months before hip replacement and bacterial pneumonia (especially Klebsiella) occurring three to twelve months before knee replacement were associated with higher infection rates.

articles.title: Intraoperative variability between the anteroposterior and posterior condylar axes in primary TKA supports a 20 degrees proximal trochlear entrance design for unrestricted kinematic alignment.
articles.authors: McPherson EJ, Kallini JR, Pena DD, Dipane MV, Chowdhry M
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty for osteoarthritis or inflammatory arthritis
articles.outcomes: Rotational difference between the anteroposterior axis and posterior condylar axis, measured intraoperatively
articles.take_home: The natural rotation between two anatomical axes in the knee varies widely between patients (ranging from 8 degrees one direction to 10 degrees the other), suggesting that knee implants designed for kinematic alignment should have a 20 degree wide entrance at the top of the trochlea (the groove that guides the kneecap) to ensure the kneecap tracks properly in all patients.

articles.title: Utilisation of total hip arthroplasty in the United States by settlement type: is there equity of access?
articles.authors: Huffman N, Oyem PC, Runsewe OI, Ramos MS, Pasqualini I, Khan ST, et al.
articles.study_type: Observational analysis of national healthcare database
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgeons performing total hip arthroplasty in the United States
articles.sample_size: 4096 to 4694 surgeons over the study period
articles.outcomes: Number of surgeons and volume of total hip arthroplasties performed by settlement type (urban, micropolitan, small town, rural) from 2013 to 2020
articles.take_home: Most hip replacement surgery happens in cities (88%), with very little in rural areas (0.4%), even though 20% of Americans live in rural areas. The mismatch between where people live and where surgery is available suggests unequal access to hip replacement treatment.

articles.title: Conversion Total Hip Arthroplasty Following Prior Internal Fixation: A Comparison with Primary and Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Hali K, Manzo MA, Entezari B, Ravi B, Lex JR
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing conversion total hip arthroplasty following prior femoral or acetabular fracture fixation
articles.sample_size: 148 patients in each group (conversion, primary, and revision total hip arthroplasty)
articles.outcomes: Reoperation rates, transfusion requirements, operative duration, length of hospital stay, and revision-free survival
articles.take_home: Conversion hip replacement after previous fracture fixation has higher risks than primary hip replacement but similar risks to revision hip replacement, with longer operative times and more blood transfusions needed. The study shows conversion hip replacement should be treated as its own category when planning surgery and discussing outcomes with patients.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Patient Satisfaction and the Degree of Valgus Deformity in Lateral Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty at a Mean 3-Year Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Long G, Yuan L, Qing L, Guanglei C, Jian L, Ye H
articles.population: Patients with lateral compartment osteoarthritis undergoing fixed-bearing lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 62 patients (35 mild valgus, 16 moderate valgus, 11 severe valgus)
articles.outcomes: Patient satisfaction, Oxford Knee Score, radiographic alignment, complications, and functional improvement at mean 35 months follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients with moderate valgus deformity (6 to 12 degrees) had the best outcomes after lateral knee replacement, with 75% reporting high satisfaction compared to only 9% in those with severe deformity. Those with severe valgus deformity had the most complications and persistent problems with instability.

articles.title: Kneeling After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Does Resurfacing the Patella Affect the Ability to Kneel?
articles.authors: Hohmann AL, Bash H, DeSimone CA, Fraval A, Lonner JH
articles.population: Patients who had total knee replacement at least one year prior to the survey
articles.sample_size: 363 knees (132 without patellar arthritis and unresurfaced; 110 with patellar arthritis and resurfaced; 121 without patellar arthritis and resurfaced)
articles.outcomes: Ability to kneel before and after surgery, pain with kneeling on different surfaces, satisfaction with kneeling ability, and knee outcome scores
articles.take_home: All patients reported worsening ability to kneel after knee replacement, but remained mostly satisfied. Patients without pre-existing patellar arthritis who had their kneecap resurfaced reported greater dissatisfaction with kneeling than those who did not have resurfacing.

articles.title: Automated impaction in uncemented total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Brkljac M, Bandeira E, Sharma S, Guevel B, Cobb J, Logishetty K
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary uncemented total hip replacement
articles.sample_size: 2,607 hip replacements across five studies (2,377 in meta-analysis)
articles.outcomes: Intraoperative periprosthetic femoral fractures and operating time
articles.take_home: Automated impaction systems did not reduce the risk of femoral fractures or shorten operating time compared with manual impaction during hip replacement surgery. The safety and efficiency of the procedure may depend more on how well the implant fits the patient's bone and correct sizing rather than the impaction method used.

articles.title: Association between surgically treated knee injury and knee arthroplasty: an explorative study based on Finnish nationwide register-based data.
articles.authors: Heikkila O, Sund R, Kroger H, Jaroma A, Sirola J
articles.population: Finnish residents aged 15-99 years who underwent surgery for knee injuries between 1986 and 2024, compared to controls without knee injury
articles.sample_size: 2,163 knee replacements in fracture surgery cohort; 13,570 in non-fracture injury surgery cohort; 205,440 in control population
articles.outcomes: Incidence of knee replacement surgery following surgically treated knee injuries, stratified by age and injury type
articles.take_home: People who have surgery for knee injuries have a higher risk of needing a knee replacement later, with the greatest excess risk in younger people aged 15-54 years. Those with non-fracture knee injuries had nearly 4 times the risk of knee replacement compared to the general population, whilst those with fracture injuries had about twice the risk.

articles.title: Dual mobility versus standard cups in total hip replacement for displaced femoral neck fractures (Duality): an international, multicentre, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.authors: Hailer NP, Griffin XL, Mukka S, Lakic TG, Appelbe D, Skoldenberg O, et al.
articles.population: People aged 65 years or older with a displaced femoral neck fracture treated with total hip replacement at hospitals in Sweden and the UK
articles.outcomes: Dislocation of the hip joint within 1 year requiring closed reduction or open surgery
articles.take_home: Dual mobility hip replacements reduced dislocation rates to 1.3% compared with 4.2% for standard replacements in older people with hip fractures. This means dual mobility implants are substantially better at keeping the hip joint stable after this type of surgery.

articles.title: Integrating Robotic-Assisted Arthroplasty into Orthopaedic Education: The Fellows' Perspective.
articles.authors: Danaher M, Lin C, Nelms N, Schwarzkopf R, Hamilton WG, Blankstein M
articles.population: Orthopaedic arthroplasty fellows
articles.outcomes: Exposure to robotic-assisted and conventional joint replacement procedures, satisfaction with training, comfort performing procedures independently, influence on fellowship selection, perceived preparedness
articles.take_home: Most trainee surgeons received exposure to robotic knee replacement during training, but felt more satisfied and prepared with conventional procedures. Those with prior robotic experience during residency felt more confident and prepared for robotic procedures in their fellowship.

articles.title: Comparative performance of the risk analysis index versus traditional frailty measures in predicting outcomes following revision total hip arthroplasty for mechanical prosthetic complications.
articles.authors: Sabet CJ, Jain B, Lawand J, Young B, Nguyen D, Hammadeh BM, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing revision total hip arthroplasty for mechanical prosthetic complications
articles.outcomes: 30-day mortality, non-home discharge, major complications, minor complications, unplanned readmission, reoperation, and extended length of stay
articles.take_home: The Risk Analysis Index was better at predicting which patients would have serious complications, need longer hospital stays, or go to somewhere other than home after revision hip replacement surgery compared to another frailty measure called the modified 5-item frailty index.

articles.title: The true fate of the 2-stage revision arthroplasty for hip and knee prosthetic joint infection.
articles.authors: Carlson VR, Herndon CL, Metcalf RW, Rowe TM, Hietpas KT, Fehring TK, et al.
articles.population: Patients with chronic prosthetic joint infection of the hip or knee undergoing 2-stage revision arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Prosthesis retention with or without suppressive antibiotics, further surgery, amputation, arthrodesis, or death at median 3.7 years follow-up
articles.take_home: About 67% of patients kept their artificial joint after 2-stage revision surgery for infected hip or knee replacements, though some needed long-term antibiotics. The remaining 33% needed further surgery, amputation, or died during the follow-up period.

articles.title: Approach-specific learning curves for operative efficiency in robotic-assisted total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Jager T, Ruythooren F, Vinckier O, Van Oost J, De Roo PJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing robotic-assisted total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 579 procedures (434 direct anterior approach, 145 posterolateral approach)
articles.outcomes: Operative time and learning curve thresholds for surgical efficiency
articles.take_home: Surgeons need about 73 cases to work efficiently using the direct anterior approach and 41 cases using the posterolateral approach when performing robotic-assisted hip replacement. Once experienced, operative times were slightly faster or similar to conventional surgery, but the initial learning period requires dedicated training.

articles.title: Short-term survivorship of a novel acetabular component with a combination of non-locking and variable-angle locking screws in complex acetabular reconstruction.
articles.authors: Guild GN, Long CW, Gresham NL, Bradham AA, Baker CC, Ricciardelli ZM, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing complex total hip arthroplasty or revision total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Acetabular component revision-free survivorship at 1 year (95%) and 2 years (94%); all-cause reoperation rates at 1 year (90%) and 2 years (86%); aseptic loosening cases
articles.take_home: A new type of hip socket component with special locking screws showed good early results, with 95% of implants surviving without needing revision surgery at 1 year and very few cases of loosening. However, longer-term follow-up is needed to confirm these results hold up over time.

articles.title: The impact of hip geometrical parameters on muscle and joint biomechanics during normal gait.
articles.authors: Aghasizade M, Karimpour M, Shariat Panahi M, Rostamian R, Kashani HG
articles.population: Computer models based on normal gait biomechanics
articles.sample_size: 45 OpenSim models with systematic geometric variations
articles.outcomes: Hip and knee joint reaction forces, muscle lever arms, muscle activations and forces
articles.take_home: The shape and position of a hip replacement implant significantly affects how muscles work and how much force goes through the hip and knee during walking. Getting these geometric details right during surgery planning could help reduce pain and joint damage after hip replacement.

articles.title: Relationship of wound cosmesis with patient-reported outcome measures following total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Masuda S, Minoda Y, Ueyama H, Ohyama Y, Sugama R, Terai H
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement for osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Cosmetic appearance of the surgical scar measured by Patient Scar Assessment Scale; hip function and quality of life measured by Forgotten Joint Score-12 and Japanese Orthopaedic Association Hip Disease Evaluation Questionnaire
articles.take_home: Patients who were satisfied with how their surgical scar looked reported better hip function and quality of life after hip replacement surgery. However, the researchers noted that the strength and practical significance of this relationship needs further investigation.

articles.title: The importance of axial rotation of the lower limb : a systematic review of measurement methods.
articles.authors: Favier B, Acker A, Miles J, de Cesar Netto C, Burssens A, Goldberg A
articles.population: CT-based measurement techniques for lower limb rotation
articles.sample_size: 7 femoral version methods and 9 tibial torsion methods identified
articles.outcomes: Inter- and intraobserver reliability, frequency of use, and validation of CT measurement methods for femoral version and tibial torsion
articles.take_home: The Murphy method for measuring femoral version and the Goutallier method for measuring tibial torsion are the most reliable and reproducible techniques, and should be used as standard in clinical practice. These measurements are important for planning hip, knee, and ankle surgery and managing various orthopaedic conditions.

articles.title: Effect of prior rotator cuff repair technique and timing on clinical outcomes of reverse shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Holt KE, Hao KA, Bindi VE, Kaiser AHA, Hones KM, Wright JO, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected database
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse shoulder arthroplasty after prior rotator cuff repair for non-tumour, non-fracture indications
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, forward elevation, and external rotation at mean 4.8 years follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients who had arthroscopic rotator cuff repair before their reverse shoulder arthroplasty had better pain scores and movement than those who had open surgery. Waiting longer between the two operations (ten years longer on average) was also associated with slightly better outcomes.

articles.title: Coronal alignment parameters of the knee predict osteoarthritis development : a Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee classification-based analysis using the Multicenter Osteoarthritis Study data.
articles.authors: Kim JS, MacDessi SJ, Lee DW, Ro DH
articles.population: Adults without knee osteoarthritis at baseline from the Multicenter Osteoarthritis Study
articles.outcomes: Development of knee osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2 or higher); association between coronal plane alignment parameters and osteoarthritis risk
articles.take_home: Certain measurements of knee alignment, particularly how slanted the joint line is, predicted which knees would develop osteoarthritis over five years. The overall alignment category itself was less important than these specific measurements.

articles.title: Incidence of medical and surgical complications, and subsequent mortality, after hip fracture surgery : a nationwide cohort study from 2010 to 2021.
articles.authors: Haugen KG, Hansen CM, Jensen SS, Pedersen AB
articles.study_type: Nationwide cohort study using registry data
articles.population: Hip fracture patients aged 65 years and over who underwent surgery
articles.outcomes: 30-day cumulative incidence of medical and surgical complications, and mortality between 31 and 60 days after surgery
articles.take_home: About one in four hip fracture patients experienced a medical complication after surgery, most commonly pneumonia or urinary tract infection, whilst about one in 25 had a surgical complication. Patients who developed any complication were three times more likely to die within two months.

articles.title: Lower septic revision rates following cementless compared with cemented robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty using a single implant design : a five-year survivorship analysis.
articles.authors: Burgio C, Salmons HI, Zepeda KE, Quevedo Gonzalez FJ, Mayman DJ, Jerabek SA, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged over 18 years with primary osteoarthritis undergoing robotic-assisted total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Five-year implant survival free from revision, septic and aseptic revision rates, reoperation rates, 90-day readmissions and complications
articles.take_home: Cementless knee replacements had a significantly lower risk of infection-related failure compared with cemented replacements, with no difference in overall survival rates. Both types of fixation showed excellent results at five years with similar rates of complications and hospital readmissions.

articles.title: Primary total hip arthroplasty after prior osteosynthesis versus osteotomy : distinct risk profiles and the modifying effect of femoral fixation.
articles.authors: Wagener N, Wu Y, Perka C, Hardt S
articles.study_type: Comparative study using national registry data
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary hip replacement after prior hip surgery (either metal fixation or bone-reshaping surgery) compared with patients having hip replacement without prior surgery
articles.sample_size: 8,643 matched pairs (prior metal fixation versus no prior surgery) and 5,569 matched pairs (prior bone-reshaping versus no prior surgery)
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery, periprosthetic fracture, infection, and dislocation rates following hip replacement
articles.take_home: Patients who have had prior metal fixation of the hip face higher risks of needing revision surgery, fracture, and infection when later having hip replacement, and benefit from cemented implants rather than uncemented ones. Patients with prior bone-reshaping surgery have intermediate risks, mainly for revision and dislocation.

articles.title: From surgical backlog to opioid burden : the case for opioid stewardship in arthroplasty pathways.
articles.authors: Jamal N, Clement ND, Duckworth AD, Collinson CV
articles.population: Patients waiting for hip and knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Opioid use before and after surgery, chronic pain management, patient outcomes
articles.take_home: Long waiting times for hip and knee surgery are leading patients to rely more heavily on opioids for pain relief, which can cause problems after surgery. Better pain management strategies, including risk assessment and patient education, are needed to reduce opioid use and improve care.

articles.title: Single-use surgical gowns are associated with an increased rate of periprosthetic joint infection : analysis of 9,239 primary hip and knee arthroplasties from a single centre.
articles.authors: Firth AM, Sian R, Nightingale J, van Duren BH, Higgins M, Manktelow ARJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary hip and knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection within 12 months of surgery
articles.take_home: Patients who had surgery where single-use surgical gowns were worn had a higher rate of infection after hip or knee replacement compared to those where reusable gowns were used. The researchers suggest this finding warrants further investigation to understand why.

articles.title: Hospital costs attributable to further fracture, reoperation, and death during the first year following hip fracture in England : a nationwide cohort study.
articles.authors: Baji P, Gregson CL, Patel R, Judge A, Chesser T, Griffin XL, et al.
articles.study_type: Nationwide cohort study using linked national datasets
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and over who had hip fracture surgery in English hospitals
articles.outcomes: Inpatient hospital costs in the year after hip fracture, stratified by complications including further fractures, reoperations, and death
articles.take_home: Patients who experienced further fractures or needed reoperation after hip fracture had roughly double the hospital costs compared to those without complications. Nearly half of all spending on hip fracture care goes to patients with complications, suggesting that preventing these complications is important for both patient outcomes and NHS resources.

articles.title: The management of distal humeral fractures in older patients.
articles.authors: Yoong AWH, Super JT, Tan GJS, Watts AC, Ollivere BJ, Duckworth AD
articles.population: Older adults with distal humeral fractures
articles.outcomes: Functional outcomes, reoperation rates, complications including infection, nonunion, instability and loosening
articles.take_home: For older adults with broken bones at the bottom of the upper arm bone, treatment options include non-operative management, surgery to fix the bone, or replacing part or all of the elbow joint. The choice depends on the patient's age, health, bone quality and what they want to achieve, with recent evidence suggesting similar short to medium-term results between fixing the bone and replacing the joint, though more research is needed.

articles.title: Time-course changes in bone mineral density after anatomical and reverse total shoulder arthroplasty : a dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-based study.
articles.authors: Nakazawa K, Manaka T, Ito Y, Hirakawa Y, Nishiura R, Oi N, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective longitudinal cohort study with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry
articles.population: Patients undergoing anatomical total shoulder arthroplasty or reverse total shoulder arthroplasty with available DEXA imaging
articles.sample_size: 137 patients (94 reverse total shoulder arthroplasty, 43 anatomical total shoulder arthroplasty)
articles.outcomes: Bone mineral density changes around the humeral component at three weeks, six months, one year and two years postoperatively; association between bone loss and osteoporosis; association between bone loss and clinical outcomes using ASES score
articles.take_home: After reverse shoulder replacement, bone density around the implant continued to decrease over two years, particularly in areas linked to osteoporosis and worse shoulder function. Patients with osteoporosis undergoing reverse shoulder replacement may need closer monitoring and better bone health management after surgery.

articles.title: Robotic arm-assisted bi-unicompartmental knee arthroplasty compared with conventional total knee arthroplasty : five-year clinical outcomes of a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Foxcroft WD, Doonan J, MacLean AD, Jones BG, Rowe P, Blyth MJG
articles.population: Patients with medial and lateral osteoarthritis of the knee
articles.sample_size: 80 patients (42 robotic bi-unicompartmental, 38 total knee arthroplasty)
articles.outcomes: Oxford Knee Score, Forgotten Joint Score, EQ-5D-3L, UCLA score, New Knee Society Score, pain and stiffness visual analogue scales, complications, re-interventions and revisions
articles.take_home: At five years, robotic arm-assisted bi-unicompartmental knee replacement and conventional total knee replacement produced similar improvements in patient outcomes and complication rates. Both treatments worked well for patients with osteoarthritis affecting both sides of the knee.

articles.title: Migration in large femoral head ceramic-on-ceramic monoblock acetabular component compared with modular ceramic-on-polyethylene acetabular component in total hip arthroplasty using radiostereometric analysis with 5 years' follow-up: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Icli C, Hesseling B, Pasma JH, Blom I, Bloem RM, Mathijssen NMC
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement
articles.outcomes: Cup migration measured by radiostereometric analysis, revision rates, Harris Hip Score, Oxford Hip Score, and EQ-5D-5L at 5 years
articles.take_home: The ceramic-on-ceramic monoblock cup moved slightly more than the ceramic-on-polyethylene modular cup over 5 years, but both types had similar revision rates and patient satisfaction scores, suggesting both are acceptable options for hip replacement.

articles.title: The Manitoba Joint Replacement Registry: validation of a provincial hip and knee arthroplasty registry.
articles.authors: Poitras C, Righolt CH, Bohm ER
articles.population: Patients aged 18 and over who underwent hip or knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Completeness and accuracy of registry data compared with hospital discharge and medical services databases; agreement rates and kappa scores for data matching
articles.take_home: The Manitoba Joint Replacement Registry has high-quality data that can be trusted for research, with coverage improving from 68% in 2008 to 97% in 2023. However, rural hospitals captured fewer hip fracture procedures than other types of surgery.

articles.title: Patients with obesity have a higher risk of periprosthetic joint infection and more frequent polymicrobial infections after knee arthroplasty: A nationwide register-based study from Denmark.
articles.authors: Aljuboori SM, Jimenez-Solem E, Calum H, Christensen R, Overgaard S
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary knee arthroplasty for osteoarthritis in Denmark
articles.outcomes: 2-year incidence of revision due to periprosthetic joint infection and all-cause revision; microbial profiles in early (≤90 days) and late (91-730 days) infections
articles.take_home: Patients with obesity had a 30% higher risk of needing revision surgery due to joint infection after knee replacement compared to those without obesity, and they were more likely to develop infections caused by multiple bacteria types in the first 90 days. However, the overall risk of revision surgery for any reason was similar between the two groups.

articles.title: Defining sagittal knee phenotypes via monopedal static anterior tibial translation. Part 2: The assessment-led personalization (ALP) system for indication and correction target planning in slope-reducing osteotomy.
articles.authors: Kayaalp ME, Kahraman HC, Erden T, Lutter C, Scheffler S, Taser O, et al.
articles.population: Patients with anterior cruciate ligament-deficient knees being considered for slope-reducing osteotomy
articles.outcomes: Identification of patients who need slope-reducing osteotomy versus those who may succeed with soft-tissue surgery alone; personalised correction targets based on tibial slope and translation measurements
articles.take_home: A new clinical system (ALP) helps doctors decide which patients with torn knee ligaments need bone surgery by measuring how much the tibia slides forward and considering the knee's overall looseness, rather than just using fixed slope measurements. This should help avoid unnecessary surgery in some patients and identify those at risk of failing ligament repair alone.

articles.title: High failure rate after all-inside revision meniscal repair: Female sex and absence of ACL reconstruction increase risk.
articles.authors: von Essen C, Kekki C, Rizvanovic D, Cristiani R, Stalman A
articles.population: Patients undergoing arthroscopic all-inside revision meniscal repair for persistent or recurrent symptoms after primary meniscal repair
articles.outcomes: Failure rate (repeat surgery for the index tear) at up to 3 years follow-up; factors associated with failure including sex, anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction status, tear morphology, age and meniscal side
articles.take_home: Half of all-inside revision meniscal repairs failed within three years. Women and patients who did not have anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction at the same time had a higher risk of failure.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence demonstrates comparable diagnostic accuracy to radiologists for anterior cruciate ligament tears on MRI: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Moraes de Oliveira G, Zotter S, Tao B, Silva ABND, Mascarenhas M, B G Leite C, et al.
articles.population: Patients with anterior cruciate ligament tears on MRI
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of artificial intelligence compared with radiologists for detecting ACL tears on MRI
articles.take_home: Artificial intelligence performed as well as radiologists at detecting ACL tears on MRI scans, with similar accuracy levels. AI may offer advantages including lower costs, faster results and reduced workload for doctors.

articles.title: Similar quadriceps strength recovery after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with rectus femoris, quadriceps tendon and hamstring autografts.
articles.authors: Pineda T, Varady NH, Olivieri R, Jacquet C, Bouguennec N, Piercecchi A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 90 patients (30 rectus femoris, 30 quadriceps tendon, 30 hamstring)
articles.outcomes: Quadriceps peak torque limb symmetry index at 12 months; secondary isokinetic parameters and hamstring-to-quadriceps ratios
articles.take_home: At 12 months after ACL reconstruction, quadriceps strength recovery was similar regardless of whether the graft was taken from the rectus femoris, quadriceps tendon or hamstring. This suggests the choice of graft type does not significantly affect how well quadriceps strength recovers.

articles.title: Influence Of Compartment on Outcome And Survivorship In Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty In Younger Patients.
articles.authors: Laing E, O'Toole G, Queally JP, O'Daly B, Conhyea D, O'Donnell T
articles.population: Patients aged 55 years or younger undergoing unicompartmental knee arthroplasty for compartmental osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: 10-year survivorship (revision to total knee arthroplasty), functional scores (UCLA, SF-36, WOMAC Pain), osteoarthritis progression in retained compartment
articles.take_home: Lateral unicompartmental knee replacements performed better than medial ones over 10 years in younger patients, with 96.8% versus 83.2% surviving without needing conversion to a full knee replacement. Both types significantly improved function and pain, but lateral replacements had a lower risk of arthritis developing in the remaining knee compartment.

articles.title: A Meta-Analysis Comparing Accelerometer-Based Portable Navigation Systems and Traditional Techniques in Total Knee Arthroplasty: Assessment of Radiological and Clinical Outcomes.
articles.authors: Tang Z, Yuan M, Jiang L, Zhao L, Qi R, Yin X, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Mechanical axis accuracy, coronal femoral angle, coronal tibial angle, outlier rates, operation duration, blood loss, Knee Society Score, Knee Function Score
articles.take_home: Accelerometer-based portable navigation systems improved the accuracy of knee alignment during surgery and reduced the risk of misalignment compared to traditional techniques. However, there were no differences in blood loss, operation time, or knee function scores at six months follow-up.

articles.title: A New Perspective On Manual Versus Technology-Assisted Total Knee Arthroplasty: Complications Stratified by Surgeon Subspecialty Designation.
articles.authors: Brady TT, Bera SR, Paul BR, Bingham JS, Grammatopoulos G, Adamczyk AP
articles.study_type: Retrospective national database analysis with propensity-score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Aseptic loosening, manipulation under anaesthesia, instability, and all-cause reoperation at two and five years
articles.take_home: Technology-assisted knee replacement performed by specialist adult reconstruction surgeons had better outcomes than manual surgery, but when performed by surgeons from other specialties it was associated with higher complication rates. The type of surgeon matters more than the technology used.

articles.title: Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty in Octogenarians is a Safe and Durable Procedure: Outcomes at 12-Year Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Bargagliotti M, Ponzo M, Zero E, Romagnoli S
articles.population: Patients aged 80 years and over undergoing medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Functional scores (Knee Society Score, Oxford Knee Score, Forgotten Joint Score), pain scores, range of motion, implant survival rate, complication rates, revision rates
articles.take_home: Unicompartmental knee replacement is safe and effective in patients over 80 years old, with 96.3% of implants surviving to 12 years and significant improvements in pain and function that were maintained at five-year follow-up. Only 3.4% of knees needed revision surgery, all occurring more than three years after the operation.

articles.title: Optimal Route of Tranexamic Acid Administration in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis With Decision-Analytic Cost Evaluation.
articles.authors: Hershfeld B, Le J, Xie K, Kelawy A, Klein B, Mont MA, et al.
articles.study_type: Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Total blood loss, haemoglobin decrease, allogeneic transfusion requirement, venous thromboembolism risk, and cost per patient
articles.take_home: All routes of tranexamic acid reduced blood loss and transfusion need without increasing blood clots. Whilst combining methods worked best, oral tranexamic acid offered the best balance of effectiveness, safety, cost and ease of use.

articles.title: Complication and Reoperation Rates of Post-Distal Femoral Osteotomy Total Knee Arthroplasty versus Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: Matched Cohorts from a Nationwide Database.
articles.authors: Orringer M, Bolia IK, Villegas Meza AD, Nocek M, Mayfield C, Barcenas AB, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty, with and without prior distal femoral osteotomy
articles.sample_size: 606 post-DFO TKA patients matched 1:3 with 1,817 primary TKA patients
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications within 90 days, revision surgery within 2 years, infection, hematoma, aseptic loosening, blood transfusion
articles.take_home: Patients having knee replacement after previous distal femoral osteotomy had a four times higher risk of infection and higher rates of other complications and revision surgery compared to those having primary knee replacement. The researchers suggest future studies should look at whether newer surgical techniques might improve these outcomes.

articles.title: Distribution of Total Hip Arthroplasty Periprosthetic Infection Care in the United States: Reported from the American Joint Replacement Registry.
articles.authors: Elmenawi KA, Zaniletti I, Poilvache H, Hannon CP, Abdel MP, Bedard NA
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip replacement surgery in the United States
articles.sample_size: 24,506 revision hip replacements for periprosthetic joint infection from 1,351 institutions and 7,390 surgeons
articles.outcomes: Proportion of hip periprosthetic infections managed by high-volume institutions and surgeons; volume thresholds for high-volume care
articles.take_home: In the United States, only about 4% of hip infections after joint replacement are treated by surgeons with high experience at hospitals that specialise in this type of surgery. Most patients with these infections are being treated by less specialised providers.

articles.title: The Effect of Mobile-Based Training on Anxiety, Kinesiophobia, and Physical Function in Patients Undergoing Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kara A, Karabulut N
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Anxiety, pain, kinesiophobia, sleep quality, and physical function measured at multiple time points from preoperatively through four weeks after discharge
articles.take_home: Patients who used a mobile app for education and exercises starting before surgery and continuing for four weeks after had lower anxiety and pain, better sleep, less fear of movement, and better physical function than those receiving standard care alone. This suggests mobile-based support during the period around knee replacement surgery can help patients recover better.

articles.title: Improving the Reliability of a Novel Baldini Classification for Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: The Development and Validation of the Modified Grading System.
articles.authors: Herold JM, Ghirardelli S, Song YD, Nocon A, Sculco PK, Boettner F
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee arthroplasty with stemmed prostheses
articles.outcomes: Intra- and interobserver reliability of original and modified Baldini classification grading systems using intraclass correlation coefficient
articles.take_home: A modified grading system that incorporates additional bone defect classification improves reliability in assessing bone loss around knee replacements, particularly in the shaft of the bone. The system is feasible for clinical use and future studies.

articles.title: What are the Rates of Recurrent Dislocation and Re-Revision after Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty for Instability?
articles.authors: Burgio C, Driscoll D, El-Hassan M, Viggiano M, Trenchfield D, Vigdorchik J, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent revision total hip arthroplasty for instability between 2016 and 2024
articles.outcomes: Rates of recurrent dislocation and re-revision for instability; risk factors associated with failure including prior spinal fusion, hip-spine workflow, femoral head size, and surgical technique
articles.take_home: About 15% of patients had at least one dislocation after revision hip surgery for instability, and 11% needed another revision operation. Patients with prior spinal fusion had higher risk of problems, whilst those who had special assessment of their spine and pelvis before surgery had better outcomes.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Increased Hospital Cost for Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Goldner M, Reddy HP, Biskup M, Lo Y, Seref-Ferlengez Z, Kamara E
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of hospital billing data
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty at an academic medical centre
articles.outcomes: Hospital costs for primary total knee arthroplasty and risk factors associated with increased costs
articles.take_home: Patients with a BMI of 35 or more, higher anaesthetic risk scores, diabetes, heart failure or liver disease tend to have higher hospital costs for knee replacement surgery. Hospital costs also increase as patients have more medical conditions overall.

articles.title: Minimal Clinically Important Difference of the Timed Up and Go Test, 10-Meter Walk Test, and 2-Minute Walk Test in Patients in the Acute Phase After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: De Leo D, Temporiti F, Guzzetti L, Crimeni E, Grappiolo G, Gatti R
articles.population: Patients in the acute phase after total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Minimal Clinically Important Difference of the Timed Up and Go test, 10-Meter Walk Test, and 2-Minute Walk Test measured on postoperative days 1 and 3
articles.take_home: The Timed Up and Go test was better at detecting meaningful improvements in mobility after hip replacement than walking tests alone. The study provides reference values to help clinicians and researchers identify when patients have made real progress in their recovery.

articles.title: Trends of In-Hospital Mortality after Inpatient Elective Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A 2016 to 2023 Population-Based Study.
articles.authors: Giannakis P, Rowe JE, Ren R, Covin SE, Della Valle AG, Poeran J, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective population-based analysis of national database
articles.population: Adults undergoing inpatient elective total hip or knee arthroplasty in the United States
articles.outcomes: In-hospital mortality rates, patient characteristics of those who died, hospitalisation costs, and complication profiles
articles.take_home: In-hospital death rates after hip and knee replacement have increased between 2016 and 2023, though they remain very uncommon (tripling for hip replacements from 0.04% to 0.13% and rising for knee replacements from 0.03% to 0.05%). Deaths are now happening more often in smaller hospitals and less often in high-volume centres, which may reflect differences in resources and experience between hospitals.

articles.title: Total Knee and Hip Arthroplasty in Patients Who Had Prior Septic Arthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Javidmehr S, Ramezanpour MR, Vaziri AS, Soleymani M, Behzadi B, Parvizi J
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee or hip arthroplasty who had previously experienced septic arthritis
articles.sample_size: 7,447 patients across 35 studies (4,896 knees and 2,564 hips)
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection rate, aseptic revision rate, overall complication rate, and functional outcomes
articles.take_home: Patients with prior septic arthritis who have knee or hip replacement face a higher than usual risk of infection in the new joint, particularly after knee replacement. Waiting longer between the original infection and surgery, and avoiding two-stage procedures, may help reduce this infection risk.

articles.title: Sagittal femoral morphology is not associated with robotic planning or soft-tissue balance during robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty: An analysis from the Brescia Knee Research Group.
articles.authors: Andriollo L, Lazzaro R, Alborghetti M, Lucchetta L, Coppola D, Grassa D, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively maintained database
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Association between sagittal femoral morphology and robotic planning parameters (femoral resections, flexion, rotation) and intraoperative soft-tissue balance (medial-lateral laxity in extension and flexion)
articles.take_home: The shape of the thighbone from front to back does not meaningfully affect how the robotic system plans the knee replacement surgery or how balanced the knee is after surgery. This suggests that surgeons need to consider the overall shape of each patient's knee rather than relying on any single measurement.

articles.title: Extreme trochlear morphology in pediatric patients with fixed lateral patellar dislocation: a radiographic study.
articles.authors: Lijesen E, Simpson SK, Lu SL, Beber SA, Matarangas AI, Tracey OC, et al.
articles.population: Children with fixed lateral patellar dislocation, acute patellar dislocation, and unaffected controls
articles.sample_size: 15 fixed lateral patellar dislocation extremities, 30 acute patellar dislocation extremities, 30 control extremities
articles.outcomes: Bony sulcus angle, cartilaginous sulcus angle, patellar tilt, trochlear depth, patellar lateralization, and tibial tubercle-trochlear groove distance on MRI
articles.take_home: Children with fixed lateral patellar dislocation have much more severe knee shape abnormalities than those with single dislocations or unaffected children, including a flatter groove for the kneecap and more outward positioning. These findings suggest that ongoing kneecap dislocation causes progressive changes to the knee structure, supporting the need for surgical repair to improve function.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Registry and Large Database Studies Comparing Contemporary Cementless and Cemented Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Lombardi AV Jr, Rainey JP, Gililland JM, Mont MA
articles.study_type: Systematic review of registry and large database studies
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty with cementless or cemented implants
articles.sample_size: Eight registry studies and two large database studies; one database study compared 1,056,492 cemented versus 26,768 cementless TKAs
articles.outcomes: Implant survivorship and revision rates between cementless and cemented total knee arthroplasty
articles.take_home: Current registry and database studies show similar survival rates between cementless and cemented knee replacements, with revision rate differences typically less than 1 percent. However, these studies are of lower methodological quality and cementless implants represent only a small proportion of cases examined.

articles.title: Impact of Combined Immersive Virtual Reality and Spinal Anesthesia on Sedative Consumption in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Druel J, Yovo A, Peuchot H, Riera V, Dizier S, Jacquet C, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty under spinal anesthesia
articles.outcomes: Intraoperative sedative consumption, perioperative complications (oxygen administration, hypotension), postoperative analgesic consumption within five days, length of hospital stay
articles.take_home: Using a virtual reality headset during knee replacement surgery under spinal anesthesia significantly reduced the amount of sedative medication patients needed during the operation and reduced pain medication in the five days after surgery. No increase in complications was observed with VR use.

articles.title: Achieving Anatomic Kinematics in a Noncruciate Total Knee Arthroplasty: Preclinical Evaluation Using a Crouching Machine.
articles.authors: Parody N, Warren S, Hennessy D, Rozell JC, Bosco J, Walker PS
articles.study_type: Preclinical laboratory study using a mechanical testing device
articles.population: Not applicable - mechanical simulation study
articles.sample_size: Four different knee replacement designs tested
articles.outcomes: Knee movement patterns (femoral-tibial kinematics) during flexion and extension from 12 to 130 degrees, measured by lateral and medial contact points
articles.take_home: A new knee replacement design with special guiding surfaces between the knee condyles produced movement patterns closer to a natural knee, whilst standard designs showed less natural movement patterns. This was tested on a mechanical machine rather than in patients.

articles.title: The Impact of Anticoagulant Choice on Rates of Manipulation Under Anesthesia, Hematoma Formation, and Venous Thromboembolic Events.
articles.authors: Crowley B, Hollimon M, Joaquin T, Lawrence J, Levine BR
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 462,869 patients (148,159 on aspirin, 123,909 on factor Xa inhibitors, 96,338 on warfarin, 84,962 on LMWH)
articles.outcomes: Manipulation under anaesthesia and hematoma formation within 90 days postoperatively
articles.take_home: Patients taking aspirin after knee replacement had lower rates of needing further surgery to treat stiffness and lower rates of fluid collection problems compared to those taking stronger blood thinners like warfarin or factor Xa inhibitors. The study suggests aspirin may be as effective for preventing clots without the extra bleeding complications.

articles.title: Coronal Tibio-Femoral Subluxation Leads to Inferior 15-Year Survival After Mobile-Bearing Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Tai TW, Restrepo DJ, Guarin Perez SF, Good KM, Carlson S, Sierra RJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial unicompartmental knee replacement, mean age 64 years
articles.outcomes: Implant survival at 10 and 15 years; need for conversion to total knee replacement; aseptic loosening
articles.take_home: Patients with significant coronal tibiofemoral subluxation (a sideways misalignment of 5 mm or more) before surgery had lower implant survival rates at 15 years and were nearly four times more likely to need conversion to total knee replacement, mainly due to aseptic loosening. Overall survival remained above 90% at 15 years in both groups.

articles.title: Cementless Total Knee Arthroplasty Is Associated With Improved Outcomes in Patients Who Have a Body Mass Index of 35 or More.
articles.authors: Misch M, Katanbaf R, Smitterberg C, Mont MA, Nace J, Delanois RE
articles.study_type: Retrospective national database analysis with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients with BMI of 35 or more undergoing primary total knee replacement for osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 91,221 patients identified; 5,416 cementless and 18,525 cemented after matching
articles.outcomes: Aseptic loosening, periprosthetic joint infection, periprosthetic fracture, surgical site infection, venous thromboembolism, and aseptic revision at 90 days, one year, two years, and five years
articles.take_home: In patients with a BMI of 35 or more, cementless knee replacements showed lower rates of aseptic loosening (where the implant loosens) through five years and reduced infection risk at five years compared with cemented replacements. Other complications like fracture and blood clots were similar between the two approaches.

articles.title: Spontaneous Osteonecrosis of the Knee Is Associated With Increased Five-Year Implant Complications Compared to Osteoarthritis Patients Undergoing Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Gordon AM, Nian PP, Smitterberg CW, Mont MA
articles.study_type: Retrospective comparative study using a nationwide database
articles.population: Patients aged over 50 undergoing total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 7,282 patients with spontaneous osteonecrosis of the knee matched to 36,398 patients with osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Aseptic loosening, periprosthetic fracture, periprosthetic joint infection, and all-cause revision at two and five years
articles.take_home: Patients having a knee replacement for spontaneous osteonecrosis had significantly higher rates of implant problems at five years, including loosening, fracture and infection, compared to those with osteoarthritis. This suggests that knee replacement may not be the best first choice for this condition and should be reserved for more severe or multiple joint damage.

articles.title: Impact of Implant Size Variation on Surgical and Clinical Outcomes in Staged, Bilateral Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Khury F, Maheu AR, Sarfraz A, Novikov D, Schwarzkopf R, Lajam CM
articles.population: Patients undergoing staged bilateral total knee replacement with the same surgeon and prosthesis
articles.outcomes: Length of hospital stay, complication rates, revision rates, and patient-reported outcome scores
articles.take_home: Over one-third of patients received different implant sizes between their two knees, but this variation did not affect hospital stay, complications, or how well patients felt their knees worked afterwards. Minor differences in implant sizes between knees are common and appear to be safe.

articles.title: Evaluating the Optimal Timing Between Staged Bilateral Total Knee Arthroplasties for Improved Clinical Outcomes.
articles.authors: Khury F, Padon B, Trudeau MT, Meftah M, Macaulay W, Schwarzkopf R
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary elective staged bilateral total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures including pain intensity, pain interference, and knee function scores; complications including emergency department visits, readmission, infection, and revision rates
articles.take_home: Patients who had their second knee replacement within three months of the first showed the best improvements in pain and function scores compared to those who waited longer. However, the second surgery carried a slightly higher risk of complications, particularly infection, compared to the first surgery.
